writeup: TIC 201429480 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.8925 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 10.87 percent dimming and a very strong signal in the automated transit-search algorithm (signal-to-noise ratio of 1625.6). Pixel-level image analysis provides additional support, though with an important caveat: the centroid of the dimming signal lies only 0.134 pixels from the target star, falling within the stated systematic uncertainty of 0.10-0.3 pixels and matching the distance to a nearby bright star. This margin of just 0.001 pixels means TESS's resolution cannot confidently distinguish whether the signal originates from this star or its neighbor. No secondary eclipse was detected, and the candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs.
